claim: The working model enforces every rule of the coin, the founder vault, the checker registry and the receipt ledger.
check: 41 automated tests, run on Node 22 in the build workspace.
result: 41 of 41 pass.

claim: The tests detect a broken rule.
check: 18 rules were broken one at a time in a copy of the model, and the tests were run against each copy.
result: 18 of 18 broken rules were caught.

claim: The report card grades real coins from public data.

result: Five report cards produced: USDC, SHIB, LINK, UNI, PEPE.

claim: The scanner's reading of Uniswap's supply is correct.
check: The scanner's answer was compared with Uniswap's own governance forum.
result: Wrong. The scanner reports a fixed supply; Uniswap states its DAO may create up to 2% a year. The card was corrected and both readings are recorded.

result: Four of five answers came back unread. The report card reported them as unread.

claim: The first pool rule and the first freeze rule fit real coins.
check: Both rules were applied to the five live readings.
result: Both misread mature coins. The rules were revised, two tests were added, and the full suite and all 18 fault checks were rerun.

claim: The name Sworn and the ticker SWORN are free for this coin.
check: Two web searches for a coin or token named Sworn, and a search for SWORN in the USPTO's own trademark search tool, read in the built-in browser on November 12, 2026.
result: No coin or token named Sworn was found. The USPTO lists 55 records containing the word. Four are the single word SWORN: one live, for worker-readiness software in class 042, and three dead. The financial class, 036, has one record, and it is dead. Jakob accepted the name the same day.

claim: A checker's reward is collected only for real work.
check: In the tested model, three cooperating accounts posted a claim that is trivially true, checked it and settled it, 100 times.
result: Wrong. The three accounts took 1,000 coins from the community pool, recovered their full stake, lost no dollars, and added 100 checks to the founder's usage milestone. Posting a claim costs nothing once the bond returns.

claim: The repository and the record page carry one ledger.
check: Two working sessions added receipts on November 12, 2026, one to the repository and one to the record page. The two sets were joined in the order they were made, and every fingerprint was recomputed.
result: One ledger of 17 receipts. The name receipt and the reward receipt, first published on the page as 11 and 12, are now 16 and 17. The words of every receipt are unchanged.

claim: The blockchain code carries the name Sworn and the ticker SWORN.
check: The name and the ticker were changed in the code. The code was compiled again with Solidity 0.8.38 in a page on app.remix.live in Chrome at 11:38 AM Eastern on November 12, 2026, and the practice-chain script was run against it. The script now has 22 checks; the two new ones read the name and the ticker from the practice chain. The fingerprints of the code and of the script were confirmed against the stored files before the run.
result: Compiled with no warnings. 22 of 22 checks passed. The practice chain returned the name Sworn and the ticker SWORN. The first 20 results match the earlier run exactly. That earlier run covered the code under its practice name and is retired.

claim: The practice-chain checks detect a broken rule in the renamed code.
check: 14 rules were broken one at a time in a copy of the code: the 12 from the first run, plus the name and the ticker. Each copy was compiled and run through the same 22 checks.
result: 14 of 14 broken rules were caught.

claim: A posted claim carries a fee in Sworn that pays the checker and the community pool, and the pool pays nothing for a check.
check: Jakob chose the fee on November 12, 2026. The rule was written into the model: a minimum fee of 20 coins; four fifths to the checker whose finding stands, or to the challenger who overturns it; one fifth to the community pool; and withdrawal of a claim that no checker takes up within 30 days. The registry was rebuilt without the pool's key. 8 tests were added and 10 more rules were broken on purpose.
result: 49 of 49 tests pass. 28 of 28 broken rules were caught.

claim: Cooperating accounts gain nothing from checks that involve no real work.
check: The run behind receipt 17 was repeated under the fee rule: three cooperating accounts posted a claim that is trivially true, checked it and settled it, 100 times.
result: The statement stands. The three accounts ended 400 coins poorer and the community pool 400 coins richer. Each such check still adds one to the founder's usage milestone, now at a cost of 4 coins.

claim: An issuer can put coins behind a statement about its own coin for a stated term, and a statement shown false during the term forfeits them.
check: The rule was written into the model: a bond of at least 10,000 coins, a term of 30 to 365 days, a first check by a staked checker, reports by anyone during the term with a 100-coin report bond, one fifth of a forfeited bond to the reporter and four fifths to the community pool, and return of the bond after a term the statement stood through. 12 tests were added, the 5,000-action random run was extended to statements, reports and closings, and 13 more rules were broken on purpose.
result: 61 of 61 tests pass. 41 of 41 broken rules were caught. Escrow equaled stakes plus fees plus bonds after every one of the 5,000 actions.

claim: A checker whose finding was true when it was made loses nothing if the system changes afterward.
check: One person ran two accounts. The first posted a sworn statement that was true. An honest checker with 1,000,000 coins at stake read the system and recorded "true." The person then changed the system and had the second account challenge the finding inside the 7-day window.
result: The statement failed. The challenge reread the system as it stood that day and overturned a finding that had been true when made. The honest checker lost 500,000 coins. The two cooperating accounts gained 249,996, the community pool gained 250,004, and the sworn statement ended as refused with its bond returned. The same opening existed for claims about finished work.
evidence: code/tools/checker-trap.js, first run on November 12, 2026 at 17:19 UTC

claim: A finding is judged against the system as it stood on the day the finding was made.
check: The challenge rule was changed to read the system as of the day of the finding. A report against a sworn statement in force reads the system on the day of the report. One test and one broken-rule run were added, and the run behind the previous receipt was repeated.
result: 62 of 62 tests pass. 42 of 42 broken rules were caught. In the repeated run the challenge failed, the honest checker ended 116 coins ahead, the two cooperating accounts ended 10,120 coins behind, and the changed statement was reported, recorded as broken and forfeited its bond: 2,000 coins to the reporter and 8,000 to the community pool.
evidence: code/model/registry.js; code/test/model.test.js; results in code/results/checker-trap.json and code/results/verification.json

claim: The launch rules follow the published federal texts in force on November 12, 2026.
check: The SEC interpretation of March 17, 2026 was read in full from the Federal Register. FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001 was read from FinCEN. IRS Revenue Ruling 2023-14, summaries of the GENIUS Act, the Senate record on the CLARITY Act, reports of the Justice Department's March 2026 charges and Tennessee company costs were read from the sources listed in the document.
result: The read sets six rules: a working system with no owner key before any coin reaches the public, no sale by the project, public statements limited to what exists and what the tests show, no custody of another party's coins or dollars, founder sales on the published schedule, and no paid volume or promotion. Six points are marked unsettled. The earlier working line for the free distribution, coins released against proven use, conflicts with the SEC's treatment of distributions given for tasks and is marked for redesign. The dollar-bond service stays out of the launch.
